critical_steps: The two-point orthonormal family satisfies both scalar identities in Theorem 3.2 for the rank-one projection K.
Its reconstruction operator is the identity, so it is not a K-dual pair.
The first scalar identity is exactly K-star times the reconstruction defect equal to zero.
The second scalar identity is the adjoint analogue and likewise leaves a kernel-direction defect invisible.
integrity.proof_basis: Exact two-dimensional Parseval continuous-frame example plus polarization of the reconstruction defect.
integrity.unproved_limits: No universal minimal additional hypothesis for scalar-to-vector reconstruction is asserted.

scientific_limitations: The finding corrects Theorem 3.2 only and does not reassess the valid full reconstruction equivalences stated separately in Theorem 3.1.
The added range hypotheses are sufficient repairs for the two scalar identities; they are not claimed to be logically minimal in every special configuration.
A nonindexed erratum, thesis remark, or informal correction may contain the same observation.
title: A norm identity does not characterize continuous \(K\)-duality
